known_limitations: C1 observed PPR did not exceed local-only on development30; Phase 1 patterns are post-hoc and must not become isolate/degree/reachability/travel-loss/auth gating.
C1 Phase 1 found all 17/17 local-rank1 cases retained rank1; the hypothesis that PPR generally harms already-strong local evidence was not supported.
Observed trace dependency is not a causal graph and selected damping 0.5 is a development selection, not a theorem or external optimum.
R mobility gates certify only the registered finite perturbation procedure, not mixing or preservation of spectral/path/centrality properties.
C5 preserves the 1e-12 absolute input-scale fallback. Zero median and zero IQR bypass relative-floor variants; affected channels can dominate numeric objectives and thresholds.
Lag3 retained affected scaler identities while L-MTL recovered strongly, so the 1e-12 fallback alone does not explain the primary L collapse; this is a real but non-decisive limitation.
G/L/ALL use common targets but different effective context/capacity; G-versus-L is not identifiable as a pure graph-structure effect.
All sensitivity artifacts are diagnostic only and do not replace the frozen primary configuration.
Public benchmark evidence is historically exposed and development-selected; final60 remains a new-protocol holdout, not an untouched benchmark.
FlashTicket target-system controlled transfer/validation has not been executed in Task F.
Historical Task D review used three distinct agents for five roles; five independently identified reviewers remain not factually certified.
